title: Core Web Vitals degrade after adding a new dashboard
description: Problem: Core Web Vitals degrade after adding a new dashboard. Solve this problem with multiple approaches and detailed explanations.

data.text: A team ships a new analytics dashboard. PageSpeed Insights scores drop, LCP climbs above four seconds, and users report that the page feels slow even on fast connections. The dashboard is useful, but the performance regression is costing SEO and user retention. You need to identify which dashboard feature is responsible and decide which optimizations give the biggest win.
Which vital is affected and why

items: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) degrades when the main image, hero text, or chart canvas is delayed by JavaScript.
First Input Delay (FID) or Interaction to Next Paint (INP) degrade when event handlers run expensive calculations on the main thread.
Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) degrades when images, ads, or dynamic widgets load without reserved space.
Time to First Byte (TTFB) stays the same when the bottleneck is client-side rendering, not the server.

terms.definition: The time when the largest visible text or image element finishes rendering. Target is under 2.5 seconds.
A replacement for FID that measures the latency of all interactions during a page's lifetime. Target is under 200 milliseconds.
The sum of all unexpected layout shifts during the page lifespan. Target score is under 0.1.
A placeholder UI that mimics the shape of content while it loads, preventing layout shift and improving perceived performance.

data.text: Use Web Vitals extensions and CrUX data to confirm which metric regressed. Then open DevTools and use the Performance panel with the Web Vitals overlay enabled. Click on the LCP candidate to see why it was delayed: was it waiting on a redirect, a stylesheet, a font, or JavaScript execution?

items: Heavy charting libraries that load megabytes of JavaScript before rendering a single chart.
Unoptimized images: large JPEGs without width and height, causing layout shift.
Client-side data aggregation that runs during render instead of being memoized or moved to a Web Worker.
Third-party embeds such as iframes or chat widgets that block main-thread interaction.
Synchronous layout reads inside chart resize handlers, causing layout thrashing.

data.title: Fix the biggest bottleneck first
data.text: Web Vitals are not equally impactful. LCP is about perceived load speed, while INP is about interactivity. If users complain the page is slow to use, optimize INP before LCP.

data.title: Reserve image space to prevent CLS
data.content: Provide explicit width and height or use aspect-ratio so the browser allocates space before the image loads:

cards.title: Code splitting
cards.description: Load chart libraries only on the dashboard route.

cards.title: Progressive rendering
cards.description: Show skeleton placeholders while charts load, then animate in the real data.

cards.title: Web Worker aggregation
cards.description: Move heavy data aggregation off the main thread.

cards.title: Static generation with ISR
cards.description: Pre-render dashboard shells and update data client-side.

data.caption: Dashboard load timeline and where optimizations intervene
data.definition:
graph LR
    A[Request starts] --> B[TTFB: server responds]
    B --> C[HTML + CSS parse]
    C --> D[LCP candidate blocked by JS?]
    D -->|Yes| E[Split bundle and lazy load charts]
    D -->|No| F[LCP fires]
    F --> G[User interacts]
    G --> H{Interaction handler heavy?}
    H -->|Yes| I[Move calc to Worker or debounce]
    H -->|No| J[INP stays low]
    E --> K[Image loads without CLS]
    I --> K
    K --> L[Core Web Vitals pass]

items.question: My LCP is a chart canvas, not an image. How do I optimize that?
items.answer: Reduce the JavaScript needed to draw the chart, prerender a static SVG fallback, or use a lightweight charting library. The goal is to paint something meaningful before the heavy library finishes loading.

items.question: Should I defer all dashboard JavaScript?
items.answer: No. Defer interactive charts, but keep critical navigation and routing scripts in the initial bundle. Use dynamic imports with a visible loading state so users know something is happening.

items.question: How do I measure INP for a dashboard?
items.answer: Use the web-vitals library or Chrome DevTools Performance panel with the INP marker enabled. Filter for long tasks and look at the event handlers that run during user interactions like sorting, filtering, or paginating.

data.title: Optimize a dashboard for Core Web Vitals
data.description: Take a slow dashboard page and improve its LCP and INP scores.
steps: Run PageSpeed Insights or Lighthouse and note LCP, INP, and CLS.
Open DevTools Performance panel and identify the longest task and LCP delay.
Code-split the heaviest chart library and load it only on the dashboard route.
Add width, height, or aspect-ratio to every dynamic image.
Measure again and confirm at least one vital improved by thirty percent.
data.expectedOutcome: You should have a measurable improvement in at least one Core Web Vital and a clear explanation of why the change helped.

data.title: Summary
points: Measure first: use PageSpeed Insights, Lighthouse, and DevTools to find the bottleneck.
LCP is delayed by blocking resources; split bundles and lazy-load offscreen charts.
INP is delayed by long event handlers; move work to Workers or debounce input.
CLS is caused by dynamic content without reserved space; use aspect-ratio and skeleton screens.
Optimize the vital that matches the user complaint, not whichever is easiest to fix
data.takeaway: Core Web Vitals are user-centric metrics. Fixing them requires tracing the user-perceived timeline from request to interaction, not just minifying JavaScript.
